item.title: Re: Cockroach Party
item.content:encoded:
Howdy hey, didn’t expect to be critting roaches today but here are my notes anyway. (Hey that rhymes)

+ Overall
- Overall

You did well with the humor. I like all the random rituals that the cockroaches are doing. I’s funny how arbitrary the lists of items are. The rest of the pacing is good too. The addendums are sudden but I like it.

My main question is about the test logs, namely why is the Foundation giving valuable resources to roaches? I understand most of the supplies, the Foundation can easily afford to give away hydrochloride acid or carrots or whatnot. I’m mainly concerned about the amnestics and the telekill alloy. Both of those are things the Foundation can’t just buy, and think of the paperwork required for a researcher to use any amount of telekill. I don’t think they’d consider this test worth it

I don’t think there’s a name for anomaly detectors, I’ve never heard of that concept before. It’s not necessarily a bad idea but you might want to think twice about if you want to do it. Sometimes it can feel a little uncreative if you just make something up to contain your anomaly. Especially because this could be contained without that by just using security cameras.

For refining the logs, you might want to decide whether these are parties or rituals. You seem to be leaning towards rituals in the logs but the impression I’m getting from you is that they are supposed to be parties. If they’re parties then you might want to add more party-like events. If they seem like traditional parties it’ll add a new level of humor. If “parties” is just what the cockroaches call their rituals however then you have the right style. You might want to make the earlier tests seem more like practice rituals and less like parties though.

+ Line-by-line
- Line-by-line

The home at 314 Crowley St. is to be hermetically sealed with plastic no thinner than 50 millimeters

I have a couple notes on this part. First, use house, not home. Home implies that it’s welcoming, it’s not really the word that the Foundation would use. Second, there’s no real reason to give an address. You can just say, “the house containing SCP-XXXX” the people reading this don’t really need to know where it is. Third, you realize hermetically means airtight right? You gave no impression that the roaches can survive without air.

Recent estimates have placed the population of the colony at upwards of 10,000 individuals

That’s around the amount they had to when they performed the ritual that made -2. Wouldn’t “manageable levels” be below that?

SCP-XXXX has displayed multiple behaviors and properties not present in non-anomalous cockroaches…

This whole paragraph feels a bit choppy. I wish I could explain more how to revise it but I’m not really sure. It might not even be a problem and I’m just looking at it too hard.

chalk was ground into dust and multiple instances were coated

You might want to clarify SCP-XXXX, because when I first read this I thought they were coating the paper.

unspecified amount, 3 kg supplied

Why three kilograms? That’s kind of an arbitrary number, and a decently large amount at that. I’d understand one kilogram but three just seems random.

When held, permanently affords subject the ability…

So is it permanent or when held? I’d suggest “If held…”

SCP-XXXX engaged in a ritual lasting approx. 45 minutes

No reason to abbreviate approximately.

MTF Lambda-6 were subsequently called in to contain SCP-XXXX-2.

Why aren’t there security guards at the location? Usually locations have security personnel to, if nothing else, ensure nosy kids don’t go inside. You should put that in your containment procedures as well.

item.title: Cockroach Party (~1,500 words)
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Draft is available under the "Cockroach Party" tab. It's about… um… cockroaches. And thaumaturgy. Idea was obtained from the Random SCP Concept Generator: "Cockroaches that must be fed magic."

http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/oystershell

Specific points of critique I'm looking for help with:

Is there an existing designation for individuals who can sense thaumaturgic activity?

Is the description expressed clearly enough to follow? If not, how to proceed

Any suggestions for the refinement of the test logs to make them funnier or squickier or more bizarre etc.

Does the pacing work? I attempted to integrate a humor->mild horror->humor progression. If it does not work, how to proceed.

Would the article benefit from Nowak being connected to Serpent's Hand? I decided to err on the side of simplicity and left it out of this draft, but if it's a funny idea I'll add it back in.

Thanks for your time!
